setup_summary.text: The next report is fiscal Q4 2026 on 2027-02-03 after the close, 94 days from today. Consensus is EPS $2.50 and revenue $249.46B. No whisper number or options-implied move is available yet.
Q3 2026 revenue was $201.94B (+12.1% y/y) and operating income was $28.08B (+61.2%). The 13.9% operating margin was the company's highest ever, up from 9.7% a year earlier.

Net income fell 2.4% to $20.68B and diluted EPS fell to $1.89 from $1.95, despite the operating income jump. Other income swung from +$10.2B in Q3 2025 (Anthropic marks) to -$0.7B, and interest expense rose to $1.69B from $0.54B.

AWS sales were $45.98B (+39%) with operating income of $17.8B and a 38.7% margin. Unrecognized contract commitments (backlog) reached about $578B at 9/30/26, against about $244B at 12/31/25. The backlog includes expanded OpenAI (+$100B over 8 years) and Anthropic (>$100B over 10 years) commitments.

The AI build-out is stretching the balance sheet. Q3 capex (gross purchases of property and equipment) was $77.3B (+120% y/y), and trailing-12-month free cash flow was -$42.4B against +$14.8B a year earlier. Long-term debt rose to $173.1B from $65.6B at year-end, and cash fell to $55.8B.

Management guided Q4 net sales to $240-247B (+12% to +16%, with about a 60bp FX headwind) and operating income to $28.5-33.5B, against $25.0B in Q4 2025. Consensus revenue of $249.46B sits above the top of the guided range. That implies +16.9% growth versus the guided +12% to +16%.

The stock reacted negatively to the print, falling as much as 5% intraday on Friday before trimming to -1.4%. Reported concerns were larger-than-expected capex and Q4 operating income guidance whose midpoint was below the $32.99B consensus. The shares trade at $240.35 against a $328.48 consensus target, and sell-side ratings were maintained across the board. Amazon has averaged a ±6.2% closing move over 8 reports and had 1 EPS beat and 3 misses in the last 4 quarters.

last_reported.text: Q4 2025 net sales were $213.39B (derived as the full year minus nine months). Q3 2026 was $201.94B (+12.1%).

consensus.text: Consensus revenue is $249.46B, about $2.5B above the top of the guided $240-247B range.

view.text: Risk to consensus is skewed to the downside. The guided range tops out below consensus, so a print above $247B is needed just to meet it. Q3 growth was held back by Prime Day moving into Q2 (about 400bp ex-shift), which does not repeat in Q4. Q4 should be modeled in the upper half of guidance, roughly $244-247B.

last_reported.text: Q4 2025 operating income was $25.0B. Q3 2026 was $28.08B, a 13.9% margin.

consensus.text: Consensus operating income was $32.99B as cited by Barchart on 10-30. This is a pre-print figure that may have been revised, and it is above the $31.0B guidance midpoint.

view.text: The guided range implies a roughly 12-13.5% margin, below Q3's 13.9%, and the midpoint of about 12.7% is a step down. Headwinds are higher fuel and line-haul costs than in Q3, Amazon Leo costs still expensed in Q4 (capitalization starts Q1 2027), memory and component costs, and rising depreciation. Consensus near $33B requires the top of the range.

metrics_to_model.metric: AWS net sales and sequential add

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 AWS sales were $45.98B (+39%), a sequential add of $3.8B and a $184B annualized run rate. Q4 2025 AWS sales were about $35.6B (derived from full-year $128.7B less nine-month $93.1B).

view.text: Management gives no AWS guide but says growth should exceed 40% in each of 2027 and 2028. Sustaining roughly 39-41% on the Q4 2025 base implies about $49-50B, a sequential add of roughly $3.5-4.5B. A sequential add below the Q3 $3.8B would revive the deceleration question analysts raised on the call.

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 AWS operating margin was 38.7% ($17.77B on $45.98B). Q4 2025 was about 35.0% (derived from segment tables).

view.text: The CFO is not guiding AWS margin and says AI mix and component pricing pressure it, partly offset by custom chips and efficiencies. Model roughly 36-39%. D&A is a key driver: AWS D&A was $9.2B in Q3 versus $5.6B a year earlier, and capex keeps landing.

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 advertising revenue was $19.64B (+12% ex-FX), depressed by Prime Day timing (an 850bp sequential impact). Q4 2025 was about $21.3B (derived from full-year $68.6B less nine-month $47.3B).

view.text: Management guides Q4 advertising growth back to the high teens, which implies roughly $25B. Q4 includes NBA on Prime, which Q3 lacked, but the company is also lapping a search-marketing change from Q3 2025. A miss here would undercut the margin bridge.

last_reported.text: Cash capex (net of proceeds and incentives) was $75.9B in Q3 and $172.2B for nine months. The XBRL gross purchases of property and equipment were $77.26B in Q3, and the two measures should not be mixed.

view.text: Guidance for about $220B in 2026 less $172.2B year to date implies only about $48B in Q4, far below the Q3 run rate of $75.9B. Either capex falls sharply, which looks inconsistent with a 14-second accelerator install cadence, or the $220B figure is stale and will be exceeded. Management also says 2027 capex will be meaningfully higher.

metrics_to_model.metric: Free cash flow and operating cash flow

last_reported.text: Q3 operating cash flow was $42.4B (+19.4%). Trailing-12-month free cash flow was -$42.4B on the company's definition. Derived Q3 free cash flow on gross capex was -$34.8B.

view.text: Q4 is seasonally the strongest working-capital quarter, with cash and payables typically peaking at December 31. If capex really drops toward $48B, Q4 free cash flow could improve markedly. If capex stays near Q3 levels, free cash flow stays deeply negative and borrowing continues.

last_reported.text: Q4 2025 diluted EPS was $1.95 (derived). Q3 2026 was $1.89 on 10.929B diluted shares.

view.text: Rough arithmetic suggests guided operating income of $28.5-33.5B yields only about $2.0-2.3 of EPS before any investment marks. This assumes Q3's roughly 23% tax rate, interest expense rising above $1.69B and flat share count. Consensus $2.50 therefore appears to embed positive non-operating gains such as Anthropic or OpenAI marks, or a large operating beat. Treat the EPS comparison as noisy and anchor on operating income.

last_reported.text: Q3 interest expense was $1.69B (vs $0.54B) and other income (expense) was -$0.7B, after a $68.4B gain over nine months. Large debt issuances occurred in July and September, including a $17.5B term loan drawn in September.

view.text: Interest expense should step up again in Q4 as the full-quarter cost of the July and September issuance and term loan lands. Other income depends on observable-price marks on Anthropic and OpenAI preferred stock (carrying value $143.7B), which are not forecastable and can run negative.

metrics_to_model.metric: North America segment sales and operating margin

last_reported.text: Q3 North America sales were $112.85B (+6%) with an operating margin of 7.7% ($8.7B). Prime Day moved into Q2, and excluding that shift consolidated Q3 growth would have been about 400bp higher. Shipping costs rose 11% against 12% unit growth.

view.text: With no Prime Day distortion in Q4, North America growth should normalize toward the high single or low double digits. The margin is the swing factor: fuel and line-haul inflation is higher in Q4 than Q3 and only partly recovered through the FBA fuel surcharge.

since_filing.text: The 10-Q (filed 2026-10-30) repeats the guidance from the 2026-10-29 earnings release and the call. The call content is consistent with the filing, and no figure contradicts it. One definitional gap: the company's Q3 'cash capex' of $75.9B is net of proceeds and incentives, while the XBRL purchases-of-property line is $77.26B. Use consistent definitions when comparing to the $220B guide.

Since the 10-K (Feb 2026), backlog rose from about $244B to $578B. Long-term debt rose from $65.6B to $173.1B. Equity investments in private companies (mainly Anthropic and OpenAI) rose from $16.2B to $143.7B. The Globalstar deal, a $17.5B term loan and an up to $80B supplier secured loan facility were added.

In October 2026 Amazon replaced its $15B five-year and $5B 364-day revolving credit facilities with new ones on the same terms (five-year to Oct 2031, 364-day to Oct 2027). The new facilities back commercial paper programs of up to $30B, which are undrawn.

New legal items since the 10-K include an August 2026 FTC and 22-state complaint over reserve prices in sponsored-ad auctions, plus a Texas suit. Also new is a Xockets ITC complaint (May 2026, investigation instituted June 2026) that targets GB200/GB300-based AWS offerings and seeks injunctive relief.

Post-earnings coverage was negative on spending and cash flow. Barchart says shares fell after the print because of capex larger than expected, slower core e-commerce growth and Q4 operating income guidance with a midpoint below the $32.99B consensus. The NYT reported shares down more than 4%. Barchart reports the stock at -1.4% on Friday after an earlier drop of more than 5%.

On slower core e-commerce growth, the company said on its 10-29 call that Q3 growth would have been about 400bp higher without the Prime Day shift into Q2. Barchart (10-30) frames growth as slower. The company statement is the primary source and is consistent with the 10-Q segment numbers (North America +6%).

Amazon cut jobs in its devices and services division on Wednesday 10-28, mostly software development roles, per Reuters as cited by MyNorthwest. Separately, Jassy told investors that the stores business is being 'slept on' (Retail Dive, 10-31).

key_debates.question: Can AWS sustain 40%+ growth, and will returns justify capex of roughly $220B in 2026 and 'meaningfully more' in 2027?

bull.text: AWS accelerated for a sixth straight quarter to +39%, with $578B of backlog (more than double the year-end level), inference now over half of AI revenue, and custom chips (Trainium and Graviton) growing triple digits. Management has visibility into 2027 and 2028 on large reserved capacity blocks.

bear.text: Trailing-12-month free cash flow is -$42.4B and long-term debt has nearly tripled. Capex rose 120% y/y in Q3, and the backlog is anchored by large Anthropic and OpenAI commitments that Amazon is also funding through equity investments and a financing facility. Those investments are marked at levels that depend on private-company pricing.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 AWS growth and sequential add (about $3.8B in Q3), the 2027 capex framework, backlog conversion and concentration disclosure, and whether free cash flow turns the corner in Q4.

key_debates.question: Is Q4 guidance conservative, or does consensus ($249.5B revenue, about $33B operating income) sit too high?

bull.text: Q3 had one-off distortions (Prime Day shifted out, advertising timing anomalies) that reverse in Q4. Advertising is guided back to high teens, units grew 12%, the NBA starts in Q4, and operating income set a record 13.9% margin in Q3.

bear.text: Consensus revenue sits above the top of the guided range, and the guided operating income midpoint is below consensus. Fuel and line-haul inflation is higher in Q4 than Q3, Leo costs are still expensed, and component and memory costs weigh on AWS margin. The EPS record is 1 beat and 3 misses in the last 4 quarters.

key_debates.what_settles_it: The Q4 print against the $240-247B revenue and $28.5-33.5B operating income ranges, plus advertising growth versus the 'high teens' target.

key_debates.question: Is retail margin expansion durable as the company pushes same-day, perishables and Amazon Now?

bull.text: Units grew 12% in Q3 and shipping costs grew slower than units. Cost to serve is on track to fall for a fourth year, robotics are scaling (over 1 million robots), and North America and International margins have each expanded by nearly 10 points over several years.

bear.text: North America sales grew only 6% reported in Q3 and International margin is only 3.7%. Fuel and line-haul costs are rising, and the company is investing in quick commerce and sharper prices.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 North America operating margin versus 7.7% in Q3, shipping cost growth relative to unit growth, and International margin.

key_debates.question: How much of reported EPS is operating versus mark-to-market gains on Anthropic and OpenAI stakes?

bull.text: The Anthropic convertible notes carry a $140.3B unrealized gain in AOCI that can be recognized through other income upon future conversions, and the 9M 2026 other income was $68.4B. The balance sheet equity stakes are now $298.8B of recorded investments.

bear.text: These gains are non-cash and not repeatable on demand. Q3 other income was -$0.7B and net income fell 2.4% despite a 61% operating income gain. Private-company valuation marks are Level 3, so exposure to a downward adjustment or impairment grows as OpenAI and Anthropic carrying values rise.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 other income (expense), net, and any Anthropic or OpenAI financing rounds or liquidity events that reset observable prices.

Operating income comes in at or above $33.5B on strong AWS (+40% or more, a sequential add above $4B) and a rebound in advertising to high teens or better. 2027 capex commentary is paired with visible backlog conversion, easing free-cash-flow worries.

Advertising growth of high teens or better

description.text: Revenue of about $244-247B and operating income of about $30-33B, inside the guided ranges. AWS grows roughly 39-41% with a margin in the mid-to-high 30s. Retail margin is flat to slightly lower on fuel and Leo costs. EPS comes in around $2.2-2.4 before investment marks, so the consensus of $2.50 relies on gains.

triggers: Advertising growth in the mid-to-high teens
Shipping cost growth near unit growth
2026 capex finishes at or modestly above about $220B

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: Revenue near the low end ($240-243B) as North America and International growth disappoints. Operating income falls below $30B on fuel, Leo and memory costs and heavier depreciation. AWS decelerates below +37% or the sequential add shrinks. A very large 2027 capex number and negative free cash flow renew the debate on the funding burden, and a negative mark on investments weighs on EPS.

triggers: AWS sequential add below $3.0B or growth below 37%
North America growth below high single digits
Capex run rate stays near $75B per quarter, putting 2026 well above $220B
Negative marks on Anthropic or OpenAI stakes

claim.text: Funding and free-cash-flow risk. Capex of $77.3B in Q3 produced trailing free cash flow of -$42.4B, financed with debt that nearly tripled. A secured loan facility of up to $80B is planned for Q1 2027 through Q3 2028. Interest expense already tripled y/y in Q3, and cash fell to $55.8B.

Customer and counterparty concentration. The $578B backlog includes OpenAI (+$100B over 8 years) and Anthropic (>$100B over 10 years) commitments, while Amazon holds $50B of OpenAI preferred stock and has Anthropic notes and preferred stock. Amazon also provides Anthropic a facility of up to $20B ($15B remaining). Maximum loss exposure is the carrying value plus future funding commitments.

Valuation-mark volatility in EPS. Recorded equity, warrant and convertible investments total $298.8B and are mainly private companies marked on observable prices (Level 3). Management says market sensitivities are not practicable to quantify.

Cost inflation in fulfillment and AI infrastructure: fuel and line-haul costs are higher in Q4 than Q3, and memory and component pricing is a named headwind to AWS margin. AI mix is lower margin than the core business.

Regulatory and legal exposure. New FTC and state complaints target reserve prices in sponsored-ad auctions. The antitrust and price-fixing cases seek billions of dollars, and the Xockets ITC case seeks injunctive relief against AI server products.

Execution and timing risks. The Amazon Leo service start and cost capitalization slipped to Q1 2027, and the Globalstar acquisition (about $10.9B) depends on regulatory approvals and satellite milestones. Satellite costs are largely expensed until the service achieves commercial viability.

Supply constraints on chips and memory. The company relies on a limited group of suppliers for AI semiconductors, and its forward-looking-statement language flags resource and supply volatility, including memory chips.

Energy derivative remeasurement. Long-dated electricity contracts (about 690 million MWh, 18-year average remaining duration) are fair-valued in operating expenses with Level 3 inputs. Q4 guidance assumes no impact, but gains or losses can be material in future periods.

questions_for_management.question: The $220B 2026 capex target less $172.2B spent through Q3 implies only about $48B in Q4, versus $75.9B in Q3. Is the Q4 capex number lower, or is the full-year figure now conservative, and how should we think about 2027 quarterly phasing?

why.text: The implied Q4 capex step-down is hard to square with the Q3 run rate and with comments about installing an AI accelerator every 14 seconds.

questions_for_management.question: How will the 2027 capex step-up be financed across operating cash flow, bonds, the $17.5B term loan and the up to $80B supplier loan facility, and what leverage level are you comfortable with?

why.text: Free cash flow is -$42.4B on a trailing basis, and debt and interest costs rose sharply in 2026.

questions_for_management.question: What share of the $578B backlog comes from your two largest customers (OpenAI and Anthropic), and what is the expected timing of conversion into revenue?

why.text: Backlog more than doubled since year-end and includes two large expansions. Amazon is also an investor in both customers.

questions_for_management.question: How should we think about AWS operating margin as AI and Trainium-based Bedrock inference scale, given the stated headwinds from component pricing and depreciation?

why.text: Q3 margin of 38.7% was well above Q4 2025's roughly 35%, yet the CFO cautioned about mix and component cost pressure.

questions_for_management.question: What explains the Q4 operating income guidance midpoint ($31B) falling below Q3's margin, and how much of the gap is fuel and line-haul, Leo expense, and depreciation?

why.text: Q4 implied margin of about 12.7% at the midpoint compares with 13.9% in Q3, and consensus sat at about $33B.

questions_for_management.question: What gives you confidence that advertising returns to high-teens growth in Q4, and how much of Q3's shortfall was Prime Day timing, the lapping of the search marketing change, and the lack of NBA?

why.text: Advertising grew only 12% ex-FX in Q3, and the Q4 reacceleration is central to the margin outlook. The FTC reserve-price complaint could also affect ad practices.

questions_for_management.question: How do you plan to balance internal use versus external sales of Trainium from late 2027, and what are the implications for AWS capacity and capex?

why.text: The CEO described a trade-off between near-term revenue from external sales and longer-lived revenue from using chips in AWS.

The Q3 2026 guidance that preceded this print and management's Q3 beat or miss versus guidance are not in the sources.

The size of the fuel, line-haul and memory-cost headwinds in Q4 is not quantified. The CFO said he did not have an exact number.
Whether consensus EPS of $2.50 includes gains on Anthropic or OpenAI stakes is not disclosed, and Q4 valuation events for those investments are unknown.

News sources differ on the size of the post-earnings share-price decline (Barchart -1.4% after an earlier drop of more than 5%; NYT more than 4%), and the price used in M.07 ($240.35) has no stated timestamp.
